blocks.text: Difficulty changes monster damage, not monster health: on Hard, monsters hit three times as hard and take only 42% of damage, which is roughly ×2.4 to their effective health. Easy is the reverse: monsters hit 35% weaker and take 35% more.
On Hard, an extra drop pool is added to the normal one (weights of identical items add up), so the chances and the "average per clear" on the Monsters tab are calculated for Hard.

A location can have **stability** from 1% to 100%. It is not a property of the map but a function of real time: each room has a scheduled "stable opening" moment (`stableOpenAtUnix`), and the earlier you enter, the lower the stability. By the scheduled time it reaches 100%.

The curve uses a **168-hour** window (7 days) and an exponent of `1.35`: `stability = 1 + 99 × (1 − min(168, hours_left) / 168)^1.35`. While the opening is more than a week away, stability stays at the 1% minimum, and entering is nearly pointless: monsters hit a hundred times harder and take a hundred times less damage.

The server turns stability into **damage multipliers**: monsters hit `100 / stability` times harder and take that many times less damage. The filter is applied when a player enters the room and removed when the room is destroyed; at 100% it does nothing.

Entering an unstable room is **not forbidden**: the game asks for confirmation ("Unstable Room", "The room's environment is unstable, the monster threat will rise significantly") and waits 20 seconds for an answer, after which the request closes by itself.

**How much Legendary Equipment Essence a reforge takes.** Each step costs Legendary Equipment Essence (`item_M315`) and gold. The base is item level × 3, each next step costs 1.15 times the previous one, and from the 7th step on there are 5 more essence on top.

**Mythic items** (quality 6 and up) also need Mythic Gear Essence (`item_M507`) for each step. Its base is item level − 3, so items below level 4 do not need it (dashes in the table), and the Legendary Equipment Essence cost is the same as in the table above.

The columns are the reforge number: from level zero to nine there are nine of them, and "Total" is the whole way to reforge level 9. For mythic items the Legendary Equipment Essence follows the first table (level × 3), i.e. every step spends both, mythic and legendary. **Neutral** items (the ones worn in the neutral slot, e.g. "Kobold Goblet") need half as much Legendary Equipment Essence (level × 2), so all numbers in the first table are halved for them; for quality-6 equipment the base is level × 3 again. Items below quality 5 need neither legendary nor mythic essence: their reforges use the regular Equipment Essence (`item_M009`). Gold is counted separately: 1000 × item level, then likewise × 1.15 per step.

**How much essence it costs to apply a fate stone (ascension).** Ascension pays the difference: the game calculates what a reforge would cost for a **level 8** item and subtracts what it would cost for an item of your level. blocks.text: **What gets into the shop.** The merchant fills the random entries from a common set, and what is in that set depends on what **has dropped for you**. Each player has a personal drop counter for every item; it is kept in the save and does not reset between runs. What counts is the item dropping for you (you do not have to pick it up), and any items count except equipment and gold. Once an item has dropped for you **4 times**, it enters the trade set with double weight, i.e. **from the fourth drop the item can start appearing in the shop**. Before that it will not be there at all, unless it is on the permanent list or is equipment. Example: "Temple Core" (item_M523) is not on the shop's base list, so without 4 drops it will not show up in the window.

**Regular merchant slots.** The number of entries is `min(32, min(10, ⌊unlocked / 3⌋) + 10 + shop_count)`, where "unlocked" are items that have dropped for you 4+ times. Every three such items give +1 slot (but no more than +10), and shop_count talents add up to +11 more slots; so the maximum is 31 slots, and the hard cap in the code is 32. With no unlocked items and no upgrades the window has 10 random entries, plus 5 permanent ones and up to 2 blueprints. The stack size of an entry also grows with the counter: `1 + min(4, ⌊drops / 3⌋)`, from 1 to 5 pieces (`⌊4/3⌋+1 = 2` already on the fourth drop, 5 pieces from the twelfth).

**Equipment and blueprints.** Equipment is not tracked by the counter: it enters the set by shop level (shop level = 1 + shop_level talents; the tree currently goes up to level 7): the higher the level, the more equipment can show up in the window. On top of that, up to two random entries of the regular shop are taken by blueprints (recipes) you have not unlocked yet; buying such a blueprint unlocks the recipe. At the Ancient Merchant a blueprint can also land in a random entry, but its level must not exceed the ancient shop level (ancient_shop_level).

**The Ancient Merchant** fills random entries the same way as the regular one, only by its own flag: the set includes basic consumables and items flagged "sold by the Ancient Merchant" that have dropped for you 4+ times (weight 2). The ancient shop level does not affect these entries: it unlocks permanent entries and blueprints. He sells materials in stacks of 10, "precious" ones in stacks of 3, everything else by the usual counter formula.

**Guild merchant orders** use the same counter: a material gets into an order only after it has dropped for you at least once ("precious" materials are exempt from this rule; they are always in orders).

**Refresh cooldown: the shop never refreshes more than twice as fast.** Timer = `base time × (100 − shop_time) / 100`, where `shop_time` is the refresh speed-up talents (the tree has 2 of them at +10% = −20%), and the percent itself is clamped to 0…50. The regular merchant's base is 30 min; the −50% cap is a 15 min floor, but with the current −20% talents the achievable minimum is 24 min. The Ancient Merchant's base is 5 h; the −50% cap is a 2.5 h floor, and the achievable minimum is 4 h. There are no other ways to speed up the refresh.

Fragments (given for duplicate items) are spent in the Fragment Shop; 10 exchanges are enabled.

**Basic attack.** The number comes from the "Attack" line on the panel: `base_attack_damage` plus everything items give (`bonus_attack_damage`), all multiplied by the "attack percentages" (base and general). Then: miss chance (evasion and blindness cancel the hit entirely), crit, then the boosts ("Damage Bonus", "Final Damage", "Physical Damage", "%Normal Attack Damage", "% vs. target type"), and only then the target's armor. None of the "magic" boosts apply here: "Magical Damage" and "Spell Amplify" do not touch basic attacks.

**Ability and active item.** Damage follows the ability's own formula: usually a percentage of your attributes ("500% of agility"), sometimes a fixed number; that is the base, and everything else is the same pipeline. Their crit is separate: "%Ability Crit Chance" (0% by default) plus the physical/magic chance by damage type and "%Omni Crit Chance", but the crit multiplier is shared with attacks (the "%Crit Damage" panel, ×1.8 by default). They are boosted by "Spell Amplify", which also works on damage over time (so on poison too), while "%Normal Attack Damage" and the base 5% crit do not apply.

**Poison: how it grows with stacks (the "stack curve").** The base is locked in at the moment of application: the sum of your attributes (STR + AGI + INT) at that moment; take off items later and the damage will not change. After that the damage grows **non-linearly**, along a flattening curve: each next stack adds less than the previous one, up to a cap of ×81:

On top of that there is a second, shared multiplier for the **total stacks of all poisons on the target** (each hero or item has its own poison); it grows very slowly: with 10 of your own stacks and 30 total it gives about ×1.3. A tick happens every **0.25 s** and is sped up by the "% poison damage speed" stat (the interval is divided by 1 + %/100, but no more often than 0.03 s). Stacks decay constantly: **−20% every 3 s** (at least one stack), and when no stacks are left the poison ends. Of the defenses, poison only goes through magic resistance; neither armor nor "damage reduction" applies to it, and it does not crit. The game's glossary stresses that **all stacks** count toward total poison damage.

**Poison on the player works differently.** When a monster poisons you, each tick (every 0.25 s) has two parts that react to defense differently. The **magic** part is `0.026 × stacks × monster attack damage` (a snapshot of its attack at the time of application): it is cut by your magic resistance, reductions and block. The **health-based** part is `0.0975% × stacks × (0.7 + 0.025 × monster level)` of (max health + current energy shield): it is added **after all multipliers**, and neither magic resistance, nor reductions, nor block cut it. 10 stacks on you already hurt.

**How to defend against poison.** "Cutting the damage" and "not getting poisoned" are different things. [[item:item_0282|Dandelion Amulet]] and its Ancestral version [[item:item_0710|Ancestral: Dandelion Amulet]] (both −99% poison damage), as well as [[item:item_P052|Poison Resistance Potion]] (−99% for 160 s, also removes all stacks on use), cut **only the magic part**; they do not touch the second, health-based one. **Application** is fully blocked by [[item:item_P051|Nature's Elixir]] (180 s, +25% base health) and [[item:item_0144|★Shadow Amulet]] (5 s): on use they remove the current stacks and grant immunity, and while the effect lasts a monster cannot poison you at all. [[item:item_M225|Life Pod]] (active "Purify") just removes stacks without immunity.

**But a "poisonous" mechanic is not always poison.** For example, [[monster:monster_10102|Hugging Treant]] leaves a poison puddle after death: every 0.3 s it deals ordinary magic damage of `0.4 × the treant's attack at the time of death`. This damage is **not tagged as poison**, and neither the amulet, nor the potions, nor the elixir stop it (only magic resistance cuts it); on top of that it applies 1 stack of normal poison. So the elixir can honestly block the poison itself while the puddle damage still goes through. Another nuance: poison from puddles and traps is applied "on behalf" of the room's dummy, not the monster; its attack is the attack of a random monster in that room, and in the Skyfall Realm (room G001) there is no such list, so puddle poison there ticks almost only with the "health-based part".

**Two traps.** (1) No more than five potions can be active at once: every sixth one removes the oldest, so "Nature's Elixir" is easily knocked off early by other potions. (2) In Endless ("Sky") the poison affix **"Realm Venom"** is a separate effect: immunity does not block it, it cannot be removed, and it hits as "HP loss" past the whole pipeline (1.2% health per stack per second, but it cannot kill: the damage is clamped at 1 HP). Neither the amulet nor the potions work against it.

By the way, the second, "health-based" part is cut only by shields and items at the very last damage step: [[item:item_0343|Jaina's Pendant]] and [[item:item_0443|Ring of Blessing]] cut the excess above a health-based threshold, and [[item:item_0291|Phantom Prism]] blocks a hit entirely if it would take more than 8% of current health (using up a charge). That is the real "poison protection" when the percentage part is bigger than the magic one.

**In Endless, poison works differently.** Its monsters are always level 6, but their attack grows with the floor: floor 1 ~530, floor 10 ~4,000, floor 25 ~31,000, floor 50 ~340,000, then another ×1.1 per floor and +30% outgoing damage for every floor after the 50th. Poison on the player is calculated from that same attack (`0.026 × stacks × attack`), so there it is almost entirely the magic part: on high floors without the amulet or a potion it wipes your health in a few ticks, and with them (−99%) only a small "health-based" part remains.

**Bleed.** You land a hit, and the game takes **70% of the damage that already went through** (after armor, reductions and block) and puts it into a bleed "pool". The pool is not stacks: repeated applications **add up**, and the window is reset to 5 s. Every 0.5 s a tenth of the remainder is paid out, multiplied by "%Bleed Damage" and "%DoT damage" (these two stats are part of the tick formula). "%Bleed Tick Rate" speeds it up: there are still 10 ticks, but the pool drains faster. Until the pool runs out, the bleed bypasses the whole damage pipeline: armor and magic resistance do not cut it, but crit, "Damage Bonus/Final Damage", vulnerability and season buffs do not boost it either.

**Burn.** Every 0.5 s the target loses 15% of its **current** health (normal monsters), 7.5% (elites), 1.5% (bosses and chieftains) per second. But there is a cap: no more than `10 × (STR + AGI + INT)` of your stats per tick, so on tanky bosses burn quickly hits it. It lasts 3 s, the target heals 25% worse, and if you set yourself on fire the damage is 65% weaker. Nothing boosts it: it is "HP loss".

**Ignite.** Like burn, but based on your attributes: 20% of the sum (STR + AGI + INT) per stack per second, up to 10 stacks, 4 s (reapplying adds stacks but does not refresh the duration). Ignite sources also cut the target's armor and magic resistance, but the ignite damage itself bypasses the pipeline.

**Pure damage.** Bypasses armor and magic resistance; used mostly by monsters and some abilities. It does not crit, but the general multipliers ("Damage Bonus", "Final Damage", "Spell Amplify") work, and so do vulnerability and the season. If the damage is tagged "HP loss", nothing works at all (see below).

blocks.text: **Vulnerability** is a debuff on the target: it takes **15% more** damage, each further stack adds another **2%**, max **25%** (stacks from different sources add up, but never go above 25%). It applies **at the very end**, after armor, so nothing cuts its percentage and it stacks with everything else. It does not affect burn, ignite or bleed. Applied by: Axe, Phantom Assassin, Void Spirit, and among items [[item:item_0196|★Orchid Malevolence]], [[item:item_0217|Monkey King Bar]], [[item:item_0344|Amorous Scourge]], [[item:item_0363|Cursed Hand]], [[item:item_0396|Stone Golem's Hand]], [[item:item_0415|Nether Visage]], [[item:item_0420|Bloodthorn Blade]], [[item:item_0503|Charge Blade]], [[item:item_0622|Star-Shatter Battle Axe]] (stacks and durations are in the "Debuffs" reference).

**Season buffs** (personal contribution level and world level, +2% damage dealt per level), like vulnerability, apply **at the very end, after armor**: each level is a separate ×1.02 multiplier, and they multiply with each other and with everything else. They do not affect "HP loss". Do not confuse them with "Damage Bonus" and "Final Damage" from the panel: those are applied earlier, before armor.

**A special case: "HP loss".** Burn, ignite and bleed (and some abilities and items) go **past the whole pipeline**: the damage is tagged as "HP loss", and it is not affected by crit, boosts, physical/magic damage, armor and magic resistance, vulnerability or season buffs. So burn is boosted only by your stats (cap `10 × (STR + AGI + INT)` per tick) and the target's health, and bleed has its boosts built right into the tick ("%Bleed Damage" and "%DoT damage"). Poison is not "HP loss": it is ordinary magic damage and gets all the general multipliers.

**What to boost it with: talents and items for each key.** "Talents" are progression nodes, "Items" are how many items have the stat and how much the strongest one gives. Item values are base values: the seed, "Enhanced" and the forge add on top.
